questions: Is the goal to minimize the sum of all entries after performing any sequence of operations (including zero operations), or must we perform at least one operation?
Can we perform operations in any order, and is the order relevant (i.e., does flipping a row then a column produce the same result as flipping the column then the row)?
Are we allowed to perform the same operation multiple times (e.g., flip the same row twice)?
Does the process allow performing both operation types (row and column flips) in any combination, or are we restricted to only one type?
Is the input given as strings without spaces, and should we parse each character as an integer 0 or 1?
Should the output be the minimum possible sum as an integer, or something else like the sequence of operations?
Given W ≤ 18, is the intended solution to brute-force over column flip subsets and compute optimal row flips greedily?
If multiple configurations achieve the same minimum sum, is any acceptable, or does the problem require finding one such configuration?
